questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar
questions.problem: Suppose $B$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $det(B)=-2.$ What is the value of $det(3B)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot B)={k}^{n}\cdot det(B).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=3$ and $n=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(3B) & ={3}^{2}\cdot det(B) \\  & =9\cdot (-2) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar
questions.problem: Suppose $Y$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(Y)=2.$ What is the value of $det(-4Y)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot Y)={k}^{n}\cdot det(Y).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=-4$ and $n=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(-4Y) & =(-4)^{3}\cdot det(Y) \\  & =-64\cdot 2 \\  & =-128.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Applying Several Elementary Operations
questions.problem: Suppose $B$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(B)=-75.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{2}:=\frac{4}{5}{R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{6}.$ What is the value of $det(C)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{6}$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:=\frac{4}{5}{R}_{2}$ involves multiplying a row by $\frac{4}{5},$ so the determinant is multiplied by $\frac{4}{5}$ as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by $\frac{4}{5}$ as well. Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =\frac{4}{5}\cdot (-det(B)) \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}det(B) \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}\cdot (-75) \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants
questions.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $X$ and $Y$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(X)=5$, find $det(Y).$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,Y=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $Y$ can be obtained from $X$ by swapping the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows. 

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.
Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(5) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants
questions.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $X$ and $Y$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(X)=-60$, find $det(Y).$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,Y=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $Y$ can be obtained from $X$ by swapping the $1$st and the $3$rd rows. 

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.
Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(-60) \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
